statement: In 16 of 16 analysed books at least one spread carries story information only in the picture; 2 are wordless and in 4 more the turning point is carried by wordless spreads (Come Back Cat, Feathered Friends, Bathtub Safari, Good Night, Monu).

scope.population: contemporary open-licence picture books: Book Dash (13), African Storybook (2), StoryWeaver/Pratham Books (1); 2014-2025

analyst_note:
2026-10-14: Best Friends and An Unexpected Adventure (wordless) reviewed for this claim. Best Friends shows only in the picture that the new friend now sits alone; the wordless book counts trivially and should not be weighed as independent evidence of the technique.
2026-10-15: Holds across all three sources: African Storybook (Bohlale: the giraffe is drawn before the text needs it; Chicken and Millipede: the size gap carries the joke) and StoryWeaver (Monu: the monsters exist only in pictures). Method rule m005 still applies: today's product is text and audio, so this is evidence for the illustrated product and for what text must carry when pictures are absent. Re-read 2026-10-15 measured only_in_image at 58% on 12 pages (below the 20-page threshold, still measuring); judging it now as information a listener without pictures would lose.

magicpaper.suggested: Hypothesis for illustrated stories: leave one fact per story to the picture; not applicable to text-only stories.
